A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching datasets, analytical procedures, and identifiable retained experiments. All 27 pages of v2 and 25 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies limit some interpretations but do not prevent comparing the documents.

before.justification: v2 reports original multilingual caption analyses, human captioning and translation evaluations, and GIT finetuning experiments, including additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 reports original caption analyses, human evaluations, and finetuning results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–B. Retained results still qualify as original empirical work.

M1.justification: The work retains GPT-4 translation, FLAN-T5 scene-graph parsing, WordNet and embedding-based canonicalization, and GIT finetuning. The multilingual prompting procedure is also retained. Revised evaluation coverage, metric selection, and explanations do not establish a changed model or algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 excludes Japanese from the main LLaVA caption analyses, reducing that source from six languages and 64.8k captions to five languages and 54k captions. Korean was already excluded. Crossmodal, Visual Genome, the overall seven-language coverage, and the American/Japanese human studies remain.

E2.justification: v2 Section 3.1 identifies GIT and BLIP2 as English comparators. v3 Section 3.2 and Table 14 retain that pair, but Section 4.2 instead names and cites BLIP (2022). The supplied PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a comparator replacement or a naming/citation error.

E3.justification: v3 reports Crossmodal embedding comparisons using caption triplets, whereas v2 Table 4 explicitly uses pairs. It removes the color/Delta-E evaluation metric and additionally reports evaluating finetuned models with default loss. The principal SPICE evaluation, 1.8k/1.8k training–test split, and human-study sizes remain. These reported protocol changes do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 removes v2’s object-normalized graph-growth analysis (Figure 5) and GPT-4 vision caption case study (Table 19), and reduces the Visual Genome omission examples from eight to five. It adds scene-graph examples across six images in Figure 5. The central multimodel, groundedness, human-captioning, and translation-artifact checks are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 6 explicitly documents multiple-comparison correction for ground-truth coverage comparisons; corresponding v3 Table 3 omits that statistical reporting. Bonferroni correction for multimodel intersections and the translation-quality summary of 4.68 ± 0.60 remain. Neither version supplies additional repeated-run or seed information.

E6.justification: v3 adds Crossmodal scene-graph results and revises substantial portions of the coverage results. Vertex ground-truth coverage for English and English/French/Chinese changes from 18.3% and 20.0% in v2 Table 6 to 9.6% and 11.7% in v3 Table 3. Headline object/attribute increases change from 21.8%/27.1% to 29.9%/46.0%. Japanese LLaVA, color, and several supplementary result entries disappear. Finetuning scores are retained apart from rounding. These are reported result revisions, not established same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The formal finetuning criterion changes from L(A;A) > L(B;A) in v2 Section 4 to L(A;A) ≪ L(B;A) in v3 Section 3.1, while v3 introduces a higher-is-better score S. This changes the mathematical statement, although the remaining S/L inconsistency prevents treating it as a clean correction. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the headline contribution from improving visual representations to documenting cultural and linguistic heterogeneity in datasets and models. The central claims of richer multilingual captions and language-matched finetuning performance remain. The color-diversity claim in v2’s introduction is removed.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations for English translation and concrete recommendations concerning annotator metadata, native-language captions, and culturally diverse evaluation. It qualifies system and robustness benefits as possibilities. Its shortened limitations omit v2 Appendix B’s explicit concerns about biased semantic proxies, translation errors and cost, and experimental-design confounds. These additions and removals substantially change the interpretation and qualifications, beyond relocating much of v2 Appendix A.

D1.justification: v3 adds that concept canonicalization errs toward merging, but removes Prolific as the recruitment source and drops v2’s parser-availability footnote and FACTUAL reference. Translation and multilingual prompting instructions remain. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes or withdrawal of resources.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises the positioning: v3 distinguishes perceptual differences for identical images from geographically diverse imagery and culturally specific knowledge, and contrasts demographic patterns with individual personalization. It adds substantial literature on CCUB/SCoFT, personalization, translation, multilingual representations, and linguistic expression, while removing several earlier motivation references. This exceeds bibliographic or citation-style editing.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and related work are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into language-level and model-level evaluations; finetuning is integrated into that structure. Discussion and limitations move from appendices into a substantially revised Section 6, and the appendices are reorganized into experimental details and supplementary evidence.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout, restructures results into tables comparing caption sources, and adds the rotated overview Table 11. The cumulative-growth figure moves to the appendix, normalized plots disappear, and caption-example tables are removed or trimmed. New Figure 5 presents scene-graph grids across three pages. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 improves organization, explains translation controls more fully, and supplies actionable recommendations. However, v2 Table 2’s 4.31 objects for Vertex English/French/Chinese becomes 4.13 in v3 Table 1 while remaining 4.31 in Table 13, without an explained setting difference. Table 1’s monolingual attribute average of 1.98 also exceeds every listed constituent value. These quantitative inconsistencies and omitted measurement/design limitations coexist with clearer exposition and additional results, making the net quality direction uncertain.
